\begin{bankq}[id=SII12-P1-MATH-S3-Q10, source={Score-II - Test 12 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=10, type=single, subtopic={Lines}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: distance from a line to planes containing another line | steps: planes through l1; distance of the line l2 from the plane as a function of the normal; maximise; compute the distances asked}]
Let $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ be the lines $\vec r_1=\lambda(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)$ and $\vec r_2=(\hat j-\hat k)+\mu(\hat i+\hat k)$, respectively. Let X be the set of all the planes H that contain the line $\ell_1$. For a plane H, let d(H) denote the smallest possible distance between the points of $\ell_2$ and H. Let $H_0$ be plane in X for which $d(H_0)$ is the maximum value of d(H) as H varies over all planes in X.\\
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|c|p{4.3cm}|c|l|}
\hline
\multicolumn{2}{|c|}{List-I} & \multicolumn{2}{c|}{List-II} \\
\hline
(P) & The value of $d(H_0)$ is & (1) & 0 \\
\hline
(Q) & The distance of the point (0,1,2) from $H_0$ is & (2) & $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$ \\
\hline
(R) & The distance of origin from $H_0$ is & (3) & $\sqrt3$ \\
\hline
(S) & The distance of origin from the point of intersection of planes y = z, x = 1 and $H_0$ is & (4) & $\sqrt2$ \\
\hline
 & & (5) & $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The correct option is:
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{P$\to$2;Q$\to$4;R$\to$5;S$\to$3}
\opt{B}{P$\to$5;Q$\to$4;R$\to$1;S$\to$3}
\opt{C}{P$\to$2;Q$\to$3;R$\to$1;S$\to$2}
\opt{D}{P$\to$5;Q$\to$3;R$\to$4;S$\to$2}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{There is a triangle whose area is 2 sq. unit \& all vertices are from S.}
\opt{B}{There are two distinct points L and M in T such that each point on the line segment LM is also in T.}
\opt{C}{There are infinitely many rectangles of perimeter 48, two of whose vertices are from S and the other two vertices are from T.}
\opt{D}{There is a square of perimeter 48, two of whose vertices are from S and the other two vertices are from T.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
